title: Correct junta node decision
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let $P$ be a finite set of coordinates in $	ext{Fin}(n)$, and let $z$ assign signs to the coordinates in $P$. A decision declaring a constant sign is correct exactly when the restriction of $f$ obtained by fixing $P$ according to $z$ is constantly that sign; a decision to split on a coordinate outside $P$ is correct exactly when there are two assignments to the remaining coordinates that agree everywhere except at that coordinate and give different values of the restriction.
